subject: Meteorology
title: Buoyancy and Convection
description: Learn Buoyancy and Convection in one minute.

hook.text: A hot-air balloon rises because warm air is less dense than the cooler air around it—that's buoyancy.

buildup.text: In the atmosphere, parcels of warm air behave the same way—they accelerate upward if lighter than surroundings.

discovery.text: The buoyancy force depends on the temperature difference between the parcel and its environment.

twist.text: Moisture makes air lighter—water vapor is less dense than nitrogen or oxygen, boosting buoyancy further.

climax.text: This is why humid tropical air produces the tallest thunderstorms—moisture adds extra lift on top of heat.

punchline.text: Wet air is lighter than dry air—counterintuitive but true.

quiz.question: Why does moisture increase buoyancy?
options: Water vapor is denser than nitrogen
Water vapor is less dense than nitrogen and oxygen
